passage:
After several bad air days, the school installed air filters in classrooms. Some students expected the rooms to feel different immediately, but the change was not obvious.
The science teacher used a sensor to measure particles before and after the filters were turned on. The numbers dropped.
Students learned that some improvements cannot be felt right away. They need measurement.
The filters also required maintenance. If they were not cleaned or replaced, they would stop working well.
The class understood that safety devices are not one-time solutions. They are promises that must be kept.
Clean air may be invisible, but the work to protect it must be regular and visible.
